articleTitle: Security with 3-Pulse Differential Phase Shift Quantum Key Distribution
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: 3-pulse DPS-QKD offers enhanced security compared to conventional DPS-QKD by decreasing the learning rate of an eavesdropper and unmasking her presence with an increased error rate upon application of intercept and resend attack. The probability of getting one bit of sifted key information using beamsplitter attack also reduces by 25% in our implentation compared to normal DPS.

articleTitle: SPR Gas Sensor Using Bimetallic Structure Based on Gold Grating-Aluminum Film
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We propose a bimetallic Au-Al based SPR sensor. FWHM of SPR curve of conventional Au grating based sensor could be reduced by using the proposed bimetallic structure and thereby improving the resolution. Sensitivity of the proposed sensor is 191°/RIU with an FWHM of 0.26°.

articleTitle: Effect of Junction Profile on the Phase and Loss Characteristics of a Silicon Optical Modulator
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this paper, numerical analysis has been done to calculate the modal, phase and loss characteristics of a silicon rib PN phase shifter for three samples with different junction profiles. Each sample has been compared based on performance characteristics to show that a graded junction gives better performance compared to an abrupt junction phase shifter.

articleTitle: Mode Evolution in a Three-Core Photonic Lantern
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Photonic Lanterns are structures introduced to meet the demands of space-division multiplexing, they form a bridge between SMFs and FMFs. In this paper we have discuss the mode evolution of the modes of Single Mode fibers into the super-modes of the adiabatically tapered structure, which eventually leads onto a FMF.

articleTitle: Synthesis of Gold Nanorods with Tunable Surface Plasmon Resonance for Near-Infrared Biosensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Single-crystalline gold nanorods of average size 121nm × 8.4nm with defect free surface are synthesized with surface plasmon resonance in the near-infrared region. The surface plasmon resonance is readily tunable from 900-1300nm by maintaining the pH of the growth solution while varying the Au<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>/Ag<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> ratio.

articleTitle: Simulation of Terahertz Multimode Propagation in Parallel Plate Waveguide of Metal
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We examine the propagation of terahertz multimode in a parallel metal plate structure. In this structure, terahertz radiation propagates through the vacuum region sandwiched by two thin metal plates. At terahertz frequencies it acts as a perfect electric conductor. Different modes like transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) and multiple modes propagate which depends upon the plate separation. The TEM mode propagates with low loss. The proposed study is important in developing terahertz devices, such as sensors and modulator.

articleTitle: Exploring Plasmon Induced Transparency in Graphene Based Terahertz Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We analyze plasmon induced transparency (PIT) in a terahertz graphene metamaterial comprising of a pair of graphene split ring resonators placed alternately on both sides of a graphene strip. The PIT effect is studied for different vertical and horizontal configurations.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Fiber Bragg Grating Employing Novel Apodization Profile
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Performance analysis of a novel apodization profile for uniform fiber Bragg grating is investigated. Transfer matrix method is used to solve coupled-mode-equations to simulate spectral characteristics of apodized fiber Bragg gratings. Proposed profile shows optimum optical characteristics results of fiber Bragg grating.

articleTitle: AG Nanoparticles Coupled with AG Nanostructures as Efficient SERS Platform for Detection of 2, 4-Dinitrotoluene
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Ag nanoparticles (NPs) and nanostructures (NSs) were fabricated in single step using femtosecond laser ablation in liquids technique. A significant increment of one order in the SERS intensity was achieved by depositing the Ag NPs in the gaps of Ag NSs compared to that obtained with individual Ag NPs/NS.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of MEMS Lamellar Grating Actuator for Fourier Transform Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Design and fabrication of a MEMS device for FTIR application is reported. The design delivers an out-of-plane resonant displacement of 98.5 μm at 30V AC actuation in finite element simulation. Device fabrication is carried out and the characterization is in progress.

articleTitle: Asymmetric-Pulse Shaping Technique Using Fiber Bragg Grating
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We report a novel optical pulse shaping technique for generating a reverse sawtooth pulse from an optical gaussian pulse using a linearly chirped fiber Bragg grating. We have carried out simulations with gaussian pulses of order 2, 4 and 8 and the results show that asymmetry of the reflected pulse increases with the order of input gaussian pulse.

articleTitle: Effect of Moth-Eye Antireflective Coatings in Extraction of Far Field Intensity of an Organic Light Emitting Diode (OLED)
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this work, the OLED is modelled using Moth-eye Anti Reflective coatings to extract maximum far field intensity compared to Conventional OLED. Finite difference time domain method is used to simulate the OLED structure. The presented structure shows maximum far field intensity of 3.6μ <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">V/m.</sub>

articleTitle: High Resolution and Wide Field Microscopy Using Fourier Ptychography and Flatbed Scanner
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We report the development of high resolution and wide field of view microscopy using a programmable 8×8 LED array and a flatbed scanner. The LEDs are illuminated sequentially and analyzed using Fourier Ptychography algorithm to generate high resolution image of the sample.

articleTitle: Second Harmonic Generation in Planar Waveguides Using Slant Grating
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this paper, we analyze second harmonic generation in a planar KTP waveguide with fundamental wave and second harmonic wave being non collinear with phase matching being satisfied using slant quasi phase matching gratings. It is shown that for the same input power and length of the device, the proposed design has greater efficiency and similar bandwidth as compared to bulk and larger bandwidth as compared to the channel waveguide.

articleTitle: A Minimum Sub-Carrier Path RSA in Spectrum-Sliced Elastic Optical Path Networks
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) technology provides an opportunity for efficient resource utilization in optical networks. To utilize the spectrum efficiently SLICE architecture has been recently introduced. This architecture helps in allocation of different size wavelength resource allocations and also multiple date rate traffic allocations is possible. In SLICE networks routing and spectrum allocation problem is a current research issue. In this paper, an online version of RSA problem is addressed and provides two algorithms such as MSCP and MKSP algorithms for arbitrary mesh network topologies and is implemented on the 8-node ring and 14-node NSF networks. The effectiveness of the algorithms is measured with simulation by varying total number of requests and maximum demand in terms of number of sub-carriers.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Directed Energy Systems Using Single and Multi-Mode Fiber Lasers
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We report comparative studies of different single-mode (SM) and multi-mode (MM) types of fiber laser sources suitable for directed energy systems. Propagation of laser from 1 to 3 km range has been studied while taking into account the effect of laser beam quality (M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> parameter) along with atmospheric attenuation and turbulence.

articleTitle: Quasi-CW Propagation of Similaritons Through Dispersion Oscillating Bragg Fiber at 2.8 μM
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We report stable propagation of parabolic pulses with GHz range of repetition rate along with the characteristic linear chirp over few meters long chalcogenide glass based dispersion oscillating Bragg fiber [1] at 2.8 μm,

articleTitle: Fiber Between Two Concatenated Long Period Gratings as an Interferometric Sensor: Analysis and Optimization
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: An interferometric refractive index sensor based on use of a fiber segment between two concatenated LPGs as the sensing probe is proposed. A sensitivity of 670 nm/RIU can be obtained in the refractive index range of 1.33 to 135.

articleTitle: Femtosecond Ablation Studies on (LuBi)3FesO12(BLIG) Epitaxial Film
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We report on the variation of the laser beam and the velocity of the xy stage to obtain the optimum surface roughness and repeatability in ablation of ferrite (LuBi)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eSO12</sub>(BLIG) and obtain a 1D magnonic waveguide of period 30 μm by fs machining.

articleTitle: In-Vivo Quantitative Assessment of Wounds Healing Using Optical Coherence Tomography
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: An optical coherence tomography (OCT) imaging modality is used to demonstrate for the classification of wound healing process using quantitative features of skin in in-vivo. Our proposed method opens the possibility of automated quantitative analysis based on morphological features of wound tissue, which will become biomarker for the removal of non-viable skin.

articleTitle: Gradual Absorbing Boundary Condition for Termination of Infinite Open Cross-Sections
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We consider application of a gradual absorbing boundary condition for guided wave propagation. We present a collocation method to implement method and consider the example of a slab waveguide. We present the effect of gradual boundary condition on the modes of the waveguide.

articleTitle: Detection of Fibre Laser Instability Using a Constant Fraction Discriminator
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We have characterized the instability of CW Master Oscillator Power Amplifier fiber laser due to Stimulated Brillouin Scattering by statistically analyzing timing information of reflected SBS pulses using constant fraction discriminator and observed a 36.6 % increase in SBS instability.

articleTitle: Light Path Switching Through Metasurface Based on V-Shape Ge2Sb2Te5 Antenna
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We propose a novel method for active switching of optical deflection angle via the phase change of Ge<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Sb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Te<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> (GST) metasurface. The 1650nm wavelength light deflects to the opposite directions according to amorphous or crystalline phase of GST in case of normal incidence with circular polarization.

articleTitle: Variable Optical Attenuator for DWDM Networks Based on Metal Proximity to Waveguide Bragg Grating
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: VOA based on waveguide Bragg grating is presented. By bringing gold into cladding region of grating, attenuation level and notch-depth are modified. Single wavelength attenuation range is 13 dB in reflection spectrum. Wideband attenuation of 0.5 dB is obtained due to metal proximity.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Theoretical Analysis of Square Knot Resonator for Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We demonstrate a new type of resonator called square knot resonator. The fabrication of this resonator is economical and it has a Q-factor of 12600. The demonstrated knot resonator can be potentially used for sensing strain, refractive index and curvature.

articleTitle: Independent Phase Modulation of Transmitted and Reflected Light via Alignment-Free Bilayer Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We present a bilayer metasurface which has alignment-free characteristics. By adjusting the structural parameters, independent phase control is achieved in transmitted and reflected cross-polarized circular polarized light. In addition, the proposed metasurface shows high efficiency up to 50 % at the wavelength of 1550 nm by using all-dielectric materials as building blocks of the device.

articleTitle: Stub Filter Based on Hybrid Metal Insulator Metal Plasmonic Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A stub type Hybrid Metal Insulator Metal (HMIM)plasmonic filter has been investigated and compared with a Hybrid Metal Insulator (HMI) plasmonic filter. Results show that, the performance of HMIM stub filter is superior to that of a HMI plasmonic filter in terms of bandwidth and extinction ratio.

articleTitle: Hybrid Lattice Formation by Polarization Engineered Multiple Beam Interference
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We present simulation results for the formation of hybrid lattice structures embedded with polarization singularities of ellipse fields (C-points) and vector fields (V-points). These hybrid lattice structures are formed by engineering the state of polarization of interfering plane waves. the generated arrays consist of higher order V-points at the center surrounded by lower order C-points of opposite charge.

articleTitle: Investigation of Temperature Dependendent Emmision Behaviour of Different Coloured Led Using Spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The paper reports the temperature dependent emission behaviour of commercially available LEDs of different colours between 40-200°C temperature ranges. The intensity of green and blue coloured LEDs enhanced by 4 times whereas decreased by 0.15 times for red LED.

articleTitle: Thin Film Sensing in Terahertz Plasmonic Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We examine sensing capabilities of the fundamental resonance supported by terahertz plasmonic waveguide comprising of one dimensional array of periodically arranged sub wavelength scale rectangular grooves. The sensing parameters such as frequency shift, sensitivity and Figure of Merit (FoM) are calculated to examine sensing characteristics of the waveguide.

articleTitle: Coherent Emission in Optically Transparent Nanoporous Anodic Alumina Films
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We report lasing in optically transparent nanoporous anodic alumina wherein the amplifying dye automatically circulates in the nanopores by a wetting process. Polarization study of the output light confirms that waveguiding effects dominate over random lasing effects in the film.

articleTitle: Studying the Near Field Capacitive Coupling in Planar Terahertz Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We investigate near field capacitive coupling between a pair of split ring resonators in a terahertz metamaterial. We examine the interaction between the two SRRs by modifying the gap of one SRR with respect to the other for different separations between the resonators.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of Nonlinear Photonic Crystals Based THz Modulator for Ultra-High Speed Communication
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The Terahertz (THz) wireless over fibre is an emerging technology for ultra-high speed communication. It is still to be realized due to the lack of effective THz modulators. The nonlinear photonic crystals based THz modulator is designed and analyzed with Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) technique. This proposed structure is investigated with the two nonlinear characteristics of materials for enhancing the efficiency of TH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub> modulator. The simulation results show that the nonlinear characteristics of Gallium Arsenide (GaAs) material based THz modulator has very low insertion loss, large modulation rate and high extinction ratio compared to Polyaniline material based THz modulator.

articleTitle: Utilization of Segmented Cladding Fiber for the Generation of High Energy Femtosecond Pulse Trains
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Generation of high-peak-power, femtosecond pulse train and pulse doublet has been numerically demonstrated by exponentially decreasing the dispersion along the length of the large-mode-area segmented-cladding fiber. Such pulse trains find applications in various nonlinear optical processes.

articleTitle: Thermal Characteristics of Polymer-Infused Microstructured Optical Fiber Using an Analytical Field Model
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We study analytically the thermal characteristics of high-index core triangular polymer/silica microstructured optical fiber with circular air-holes in the cladding infiltrated with polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) elastomer. Comparisons with numerical simulation results based on full vector finite-difference method have been included.

articleTitle: Inhomogeneously Polarized Robust Laser Beam for Propagation in Random Media
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A laser beam whose intensity profile remains robust against time varying phase fluctuations is engineered using polarization and angular momentum diversity. This inhomogeneously polarized beam maintains a high Signal-to-noise Ratio (SNR) at the detector without any need of active correction methods.

articleTitle: Remote Control of Liquid Crystal Elastomer Random Laser
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We demonstrate random lasing in a composite system fabricated from elastomeric liquid crystals and TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2 </sub>nanoparticles. By moving this random laser near the focal plane of the pump beam, we achieve control of its emission properties.

articleTitle: Self-Cleaning Femtosecond Laser Micromachining of Grooves on Silicon: Effect of Solvent Immersion
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In micromachining, the extruded material is redeposited back on the structured surface. In this work, we report on the advantages and results of fs laser-based surface micromachining of methanol immersed of Si comparing the same with the ambient air.

articleTitle: Analytical Study of Clad Waveguide Sensor with Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We analyzed a metal clad waveguide sensor with metamaterial guiding layer. Enhanced values of sensitivity are obtained for proposed sensor in comparison to existing conventional sensors. Proposed sensor has larger sensitivity, which is very much applicable for biological sensing.

articleTitle: Temperature Varied Photonic Crystal Fiber for Two-Stage Non-Integer Soliton Compression
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Temperature variation along the length of the photonic crystal fiber is considered for compressing non-integer soliton of order 2.8. Two-stage soliton compression is presented and we get a high compression factor of 25 with no splice loss.

articleTitle: Design and Modelling of SCISSOR Structure for Nanophotonic Integrated Delay Lines
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We present design and modelling of a five ring SCISSOR structure. The proposed device structure is analyzed mathematically and modelled based on FDTD simulation tool. The miniaturized dimensions of the proposed structure can enable on-chip nanophotonic integration for delay line applications.

articleTitle: Diffraction of Zero Topological Index V-Point Singular Beams
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: V-points are polarization singularities in linearly polarized optical fields characterized by topological index or Poincare-Hopf index which takes integer values, including zero. The diffraction of integer valued V-points are straight forward and a V-point disintegrates into two C-points upon diffraction. Here we report the diffraction of zero topological index V-points, having different spatial polarization distributions, through circular and triangular apertures. The diffracted filed, at the focal region of a converging lens, show some interesting intensity distributions when decomposed the total field into linear and circular orthogonal state of polarization.

articleTitle: Fabrication of CR: Yagdoped Silica Optical Fiber Using Modified Powder in Tube Technique
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Fabrication of Cr-YAG doped silica optical fiber suitable for tunable laser source using a modified powder in tube technique is reported for the first time. Initial performance along with its optical and material characterization is also presented.

articleTitle: Bend Insensitive YB-Doped Fiber Fabricated Through Vapour Phase Doping Process
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Bend insensitive newly designed Yb doped silica fiber fabricated using vapor phase doping technique is presented. It exhibits improved transmission characteristics compared to step-index and depressed clad fiber with similar Yb-concentration, besides showing excellent lasing amplification characteristics.

articleTitle: Numerical Study of the Output Characteristics of a Multi-Electrode Semiconductor Laser
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A numerical approach based on the established model to study the output characteristics of a multi-electrode semiconductor laser has been presented. The study shows that the output power and wavelength depends on the carrier profile, which can be optimized.

articleTitle: Gain Switched All-Fiber Holmium Laser at 2.1 Micron
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Gain switched all-fiber holmium laser has been designed by using Q-switched thulium fiber laser as pump source. The output power of 1 W at 2.1 micron with slope efficiency of 31% has been achieved. The spectral line width is 0.3 nm with SNR of more than 25 dB.

articleTitle: Study of Water Loss in the Rose Petals Using Terahertz Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We report the water loss study in rose petals using time domain spectroscopy between 0.1 and 2.5 THz range. It was carried out between 30 - 110 °C under control temperature condition. The result is cross verified using FTIR spectra.

articleTitle: Behavior of Graphene as a Metal in Mid-IR Region Without the Negative Dielectric Constant
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: This article presents a nano-plasmonic structure using Graphene which yielded a plasmonic mode with low loss and high effective mode area. These results were obtained with the positive metal dielectric constant of Graphene using Finite Element Method (FEM).

articleTitle: Sub 100 NS TM Gain-Switched Fiber Laser Pumped by Rectangular Pulse Er: Yb Fiber Laser and Effect on Tissue Ablation
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: A nano-second mode-locked Er: Yb fiber laser has been employed to generate gain-switched pulses of sub-100 ns duration from a thulium fiber laser cavity with a wavelength near water absorption peak. Potential application in tissue ablation surgery is under study.

articleTitle: Fiber-Optic Micro-Endoscopy for Imaging Biological Cells at Remote Location and Depixelation of Images Using Discrete Cosine Transform
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: High resolution wide field fluorescent imaging is demonstrated using imaging fiber bundle which contain 30000 numbers of single mode fibers. Further discrete cosine transform method applied to eliminate pixilation of image without sacrificing the resolution.

articleTitle: $1\times 2$ Optical Switch Based on Nematic Liquid Crystal Core Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We present fabrication and characterization of an electrically-controlled 1 × 2 optical switch, based on a Y-branch liquid crystal core waveguide, by a proper choice of applied voltage on the three electrodes corresponding to the input and two output ports.

articleTitle: Quantitative Detection of Morphological Alterations in Red Blood Cell During Storage Using PS-FF-OCT System
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: During storage red blood cells will undergoes numerous functional, biochemical and structural changes. In this paper, we determined the morphological alterations in the stored red blood cells using phase-shifting full-field optical coherence tomography (PS-FF-OCT) system.

Author Keywords: phase-shifting interferometry and red blood cells

articleTitle: Dark Mode Based Thin Film Sensing in Terahertz Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this work, we have designed a metamaterial based sensor consists of asymmetric Split Ring Resonators (SRRs). It displays sharp resonance peaks in the frequency spectrum due to the excitation of dark eigen modes which resulted in high Q factor hence leading to high FoM values.

articleTitle: Optimization of Four- Wave Mixing Based Multilevel Phase Quantization Through Gain Extinction Ratio
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We prescribe a universal optimization scheme based on gain extinction ratio for four-wave mixing (FWM) based multilevel phase quantization and numerically demonstrate the optimization for 4-level phase quantization in semiconductor optical amplifiers (SOA).

articleTitle: Differential Pressure Sensor Using Integrated Optical MEMS and Double Ring Resonator
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this work, we designed and simulated a differential pressure sensor using a double ring resonator with radius 5μm and 4μm placed on the fixed of a cantilever beam with dimensions 100μm × 30μm x 5μm. The stress induced on the cantilever changes the refractive index in the waveguide which results in the shift of the resonant wavelength. A sensitivity of 15.544pm/kPa is achieved. The sensor is operated at wavelength equal to 1.55μm and can be used for aircraft, medicine and automobile.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact Polarization Rotator Based on a Silicon Slot-Waveguide for Applications in Mid-IR
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We propose design of a compact and very efficient silicon-based polarization rotator for mid-IR wavelength of 4.47 μm. Achievable power coupling efficiency could be as large as 94.5% for both the polarization within a device length of just 0.576 mm.

articleTitle: A Ring Resonator with Liquid Crystal for Biosensing Application
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: In this work, a ring resonator is designed to study the resonance characteristics. The resonance characteristics of the ring resonator dependency on the ring diameter, waveguide width and the gap between the ring and waveguide are considered to be 6μm, 15μm and 0.1μm respectively. The resonance frequency, free spectral range (FSR), Quality (Q) factor of the resonances are determined. In this simulation, a liquid crystal (LC) is placed as a covering medium for biosensing application. Liquid crystal based Ring resonator is simulated at 1550nm wavelength.

articleTitle: Interface of the Quantum Key Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The fiber-optical quantum key distribution system with phase coding of photon states is investigated. A description of the principle of the system operation in the mode of forming quantum keys is given. A synchronization process is described, which consists in detecting a time interval with an optical pulse. The results of experimental studies are presented and the basic requirements for the hardware of the quantum key distribution system are formulated. The structural scheme of the interaction interface of the self-compensation quantum key distribution system is shown taking into account the features of the detection equipment. The main parameters and relationships that should be taken into account when developing the interface model are given.

articleTitle: Filament Induced Surface Modification of Composite Material
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: We present the role of different external focusing conditions on the surface modification induced by loosely focused femtosecond laser pulse generated filaments in the composite material.

articleTitle: Learning with Deep Photonic Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) are computational models used in Machine Learning (ML), based on a large collection of connected simple units called artificial neurons, loosely analogous to axons in a biological brain. Most of the Neural Networks (NNs) work in classical architecture and a few hardware implementations with optical components have been proposed, which facilitates real-time parallel processing of massive data sets. While these Optical Neural Networks (ONNs) are faster and comparable in efficiency with the classical NNs, they lack in scalability and flexibility. We have proposed a scalable and reconfigurable photonic lattice based NN, similar to feedforward neural network, where photonic lattice represents the layer of the network. The superposition property of quantum computations allows photons to process massive data sets faster than electronic circuits. We explicitly tried to exploit quantum coherence for learning. Hardware implementations put restrictions on the weight space of photon as negative weights are not possible, therefore we have modified the Backpropagation algorithm for optimizing the weights of the network to manipulate the quantum states. The proposed architecture is theoretically scalable as any number of photonic lattice can be included and provides a platform to get benefit of photonic lattices with different properties. It can be used in understanding the learning behaviour of NNs in a constrained environment.

articleTitle: WRAP-17
publicationTitle: 2017 IEEE Workshop on Recent Advances in Photonics (WRAP)
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: light polarisation; optical design techniques; optical waveguides; fibre lasers; integrated optics; thin film sensors; optical sensors; diffraction gratings; plasmonics; optical resonators.
